claims.text: Conventionally cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has insufficient strength for industrial fastener applications.
The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has insufficient creep performance for industrial fastener applications.
Post-solution aging can induce ordered L12 nanoprecipitates in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Solution annealing at approximately 1200°C will homogenize the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure.
Aging at approximately 600°C for 10–20 hours will produce the desired nanoprecipitate population.
The treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale L12 precipitates decorating lamellar boundaries.
Fine L12 precipitates impede dislocation motion through precipitation-hardening mechanisms.
The nanoprecipitates stabilize the lamellar microstructure.
The aged alloy will have approximately 20–30% greater yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
Retarding boundary sliding will improve room-temperature creep resistance.
The aged alloy will exhibit improved room-temperature creep resistance relative to the starting alloy.
L12 precipitates will block corrosive pathways at lamellar interfaces.
The aged alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the starting alloy.
Optimized aging will preserve acceptable ductility with only a minimal compromise.
Long-term precipitate coarsening could reduce strength and ductility.
The treated alloy can maintain improved performance during extreme temperature fluctuations, prolonged loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive exposure.

contradictions.description: The starting state is defined as conventionally cast/as-cast, but the control is described as both 'solution annealed and as-cast.' A specimen cannot remain strictly as-cast after solution annealing, so the baseline is inconsistent and does not clearly isolate the effect of aging.
